Key pillars of her day-off routine include:

•	Prioritize & Plan (01:24 - 03:16): Faye uses a 'brain dump' and the Eisenhower Matrix to clear mental clutter and reduce decision fatigue by categorizing tasks based on urgency and importance.
•	Brain Juice (03:17 - 04:19): She emphasizes that exercise is non-negotiable, noting that it boosts Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF), which enhances memory, focus, and executive function.
•	Pamper & Prep (04:20 - 06:00): A structured self-care session, including dry brushing and specific hair/skin routines, which serves as a reset for her physical appearance and well-being.
•	Mind Over Matter (06:01 - 07:29): She replaces passive consumption (like watching reality TV) with active learning through platforms like Skillshare to improve cognitive flexibility.
•	Matcha Before Mayhem (07:30 - 08:39): Faye opts for matcha over coffee, explaining that the L-theanine content provides a calm, focused alertness without the typical jitters or energy crashes.
•	Midday Reset (08:40 - 13:15): She incorporates mindfulness and meditation to combat midday energy dips and lower cortisol levels, helping her stay present during stressful or high-stakes moments.
•	Push & Rest (13:16 - 13:59): By tackling her most important tasks early via the Eisenhower Matrix, she can fully 'switch off' in the evening, establishing firm work boundaries to improve sleep and reduce rumination.
•	Quality Time (14:00 - 14:45): Ending the day with focused, meaningful social interaction to boost oxytocin and reconnect with what matters most.

I apologize if this post is long, but if you cannot bear to read it for 180 seconds, know that this has been happening in a part of this Earth for 80 years. Let’s set aside those 80 years and focus only on the last two.
In just two years:
Over 79,220 Palestinians have been martyred, not including those in Lebanon, or the bodies that vanished and turned to ash. The occupation uses thermal vacuum explosives reaching temperatures of 3500°C or more, incinerating human bodies into ash within seconds. If you cannot fathom the horror of these numbers, think if someone you love had just a single hair on their head harmed—only then will you understand.
Death is not the end in Palestine. Many bodies are blown up again after being buried; others are stolen for organ trafficking and then tossed in the trash as remains stuffed with cotton.
Hundreds of children have been kidnapped and tortured with electric shocks, cigarettes, and sharp instruments boring into their flesh. I am not talking about young men; I am talking about children under the age of five.
Gaza has seen mass graves defined by numbers. They were denied the right to be known by their names; they were treated as mere digits without value.
Gaza was starved. Food, water, medicine, feminine hygiene products, and anesthesia were all blocked. Amputations are performed on children and adults with no anesthesia whatsoever.
Thousands are suffering from skin diseases and viral infections, while 2 million people have been displaced dozens of times, only to drown in rain inside canvas tents.
Thousands of children are now orphans, some without even a family record left.
The Zionist entity has broken hundreds of truces. They blocked aid, and when they finally allowed some in, it was luxury coffee and chocolate—useless against famine. To put it simply: they are mocking our hunger.
For months, Palestinians couldn't even find flour. A single loaf of bread became a dream.
The occupation claims to punish Hamas, but I do not understand how a month-old infant can be "affiliated with Hamas" or carry a weapon to be killed in cold blood.
Palestinians are attacked by military dogs, including a child with Down syndrome and an elderly woman who had no strength to resist.
Thousands of journalists and paramedics were killed without justification.
Dozens of schools and universities were bombed. There are no schools left, and tragically, there are almost no students left—most have been martyred.
12,958 Palestinians were threatened with the execution of their families if they didn't comply with the occupation's demands.
Mosques were demolished. The houses of God! As the Quran says: "And who are more unjust than those who prevent the name of Allah from being mentioned in His mosques and strive for their destruction?" Yet, the world remains silent.
The children of Gaza now play "funeral." They have seen so many bodies that they put their toys on stretchers and carry them in mock funeral processions.

Sexual violence and rape are systematically used against men, women, and children.
Muslims are forbidden from praying or fasting. They are forced to throw the Quran on the ground and listen to insults against Islam.
Prisoners are taken as "extra" (bargaining chips) without charge, simply for providing aid to others.
Strip searches occur multiple times a day for men, women, and children. Women are forcibly stripped of their hijabs; those who refuse are killed.
Torture by electricity continues until the prisoner faints or bleeds.
Forced Prostration: Prisoners are forced to sit in a "prostration" (Sujood) position—without being allowed to pray—for more than 18 hours a day.
The One-Minute Rule: Prisoners are given only one minute every three days to use the bathroom/wash. If they are a second late, they and their entire cell are brutally punished.
Sensory Torture: Prisoners cannot sleep due to constant noise, provocation, and the sounds of dogs and guards' boots. They endure this with no food, no water, and no hygiene.

A Call to Action
The "Death Penalty Law" is not a new development; it is just a legal label for a reality that has existed for years. It is a test of our patience—a patience that should have already turned into waves of rage to save what can be saved.
Do not extinguish the last glimmer of hope that thousands cling to. Speak up. Do not be silent.

The reality is while we are “all different”, we share a common biology.   This overarching biology might be disrupted by years of eating fruit loops and other non nutritional “foods” but we all share the same core architecture.  We have differences in our taste and willpower, as a diabetic I’ve had several people ask me, when they were diagnosed as a type 2 diabetic, what to do and the most common response is oh I can’t give up pasta or insert favorite food.

I used to cook pasta multiple times a week every week when I get home from work. When they told me to cut out fat and red meat, I started eating healthy foods like “baked potatoes.”  Then they diagnosed me as a diabetic, and I realized everything they told me was wrong.  I mean, the medical professionals that were treating me.

The medical standard of care before the intervention of insulin therapy was a low-carb diet for diabetes.   The very first diabetic education class I took 20 years ago told me that and they also told me but people can’t control themselves so we just give them a pill.  They told me this right after I was prescribed metformin.

Maybe you can be healthy on an all carb diet, but I doubt it.  Your body can produce glucose if it needs it through the process of gluconeogenesis that’s a huge problem for me now as a type two diabetic because my blood sugar doesn’t come back down when that happens.  It can’t produce amino acids or fatty acids.   I think in a long-term study meat wins.  Because your body can’t produce what you get from it, maybe you don’t need to go full carnivore but you should probably leave out anything that’s man-made and doesn’t come from nature.

comments.text:
Hey! Love your videos. I'm really late to the party on this one, but i did want to comment on raw milk:

As long as you are familiar with your source, and know they take better care of their cows, ie: their hygiene, their health, cleanliness of living conditions, free access to outdoors, raw milk is actually really good for you! Unfortunately, the high heat pasteurization process kills and removes almost all the vital nutrients(and good bacteria) of milk. Then they "fortify" it, watering it down, and, depending on the type, removing fat. Also, remember why pasteurization came around. It was because of the poor conditions cows were living in when mass production came around. It created unhealthy environments for bad bacteria to be created in and consumed by the cows. Before that, everyone drank raw milk, sometimes right from the teat. Raw milk from a reputable source is by far healthier. 

It also tastes WAY better. I hated milk growing up, and once i tried raw milk, i realized why. Its because pasteurized, highly processed milk is a far cry from the real stuff. 

As Ron Swanson says, "there's only one more thing i hate more than lying. Skim milk. Which is water that's lying about being milk." 😂

Do your proper research and make the best decision for yourself first, but don't knock it until you try it! 

*Another note: there are also people who process fibrous foods waaaay too quickly, like me. Its like the fiber kicks the digestive system into high gear. So a lot of times, the food is out of our systems before it has a chance to properly digest and utilize any nutrients, leaving you feeling groggy, tired, and still hungry. However, meat is super slow digesting. Since it is so dense, it slows down your digestion, giving your body time to properly break it down, absorb nutrients, and therefore, feel fuller longer. And i will do anything to feel fuller longer, so i do tend to lead to a higher meat and protein diet. One of my meal preps is a meat heavy chili with beans, and other cooked veggies. Cooked veggies have also shown to digest slower than raw, so I stay away from the leaf type salads unless i am eating a big steak with it. Long story short, that is probably why those out there who try a carnivore/animal based diet tend to have so much success, and they feel so much better than they did on the standard american diet(sad). So they want to share that with everyone they know. Problem is, with social media, that is literally everyone. And everyone has their own opinion, lol.

The butthole sunning thing is actually wild. 
1. Yes, you do get sunburns on your buttholeand they are so much worse specifically because it never sees daylight.

3. Places in your body with a mucus membrane are places that are supposed to stay moist, such as your mouth, nose and eyes (the vagina has a different ecosystem with yeast), so those orifices can cycle out debris that gets caught in them before they can harm the orifice itself (think snot or eye goop).

comments.author: @lunastudies-p5g
comments.text:
Just to clarify, the girl in the video who said "the reason why we get sick is the buildup of toxins in the body" is really misleading — the idea that we get sick from ‘toxin buildup’ isn’t actually how the human body works.

In science and medicine, toxins are specific harmful substances (like carbon monoxide, lead, certain chemicals, etc.). They’re not some vague thing that just builds up from everyday life. And when toxins do build up to dangerous levels, that’s considered poisoning or a serious medical condition — not something that explains normal issues like colds, acne, fatigue, or general sickness.

Your body already has built-in systems that constantly remove waste and harmful substances — mainly the liver, kidneys, lungs, and digestive system. You don’t need special “detoxes” or cleanses for this to happen — it’s literally their job to keep you alive and functioning.

Most illnesses are actually caused by very specific things like viruses, bacteria, immune responses, genetics, or lifestyle factors — not a general buildup of ‘toxins.’

The problem with spreading this idea is that it can confuse people and sometimes push them toward fake ‘detox’ solutions instead of understanding what’s really going on with their health. 
I swear, influencers don't even do their basic research before saying the most inaccurate info and promoting it online.

comments.text: Bwahaha “skinny is rented” and “no-one is just “naturally” skinny”is such BS. To use her metaphor, some people don’t pay rent, they inherited a property from their parents. When I was younger I was a size 2-4 and I ate EVERYTHING. My metabolism was insane and I could eat more than both my parents combined. Like an entire large pizza by myself, and still be hungry. Some people are just built that way, like some people are just tall. Can someone be skinnIER by working out and eating right. Sure (not always as doing the healthy thing sometimes causes weight redistribution rather than loss), but they probably will never get the same body as someone who is naturally skinny due to how genetics and other factors determine how the body processes nutrients and distributes fat. Also, while “big boned” is used as a joke, there is some fact behind it, in that bone distribution and build affects the size of your body. Eg, I’m currently a size 12 and my hip bones are just beneath my skin. So if I lost weight, my butt may get smaller and my pant size would go down, but I’ll probably never be a size 4 again (while still actually being healthy) just because of the physical distance between the tops of my hip bones. There’s no “fat” to lose to make your hip bone sit closer together. Trying to shame people for having different bodies is such bullshit. You are skinny, you work out and work hard to keep it that way. Good for you. It doesn’t mean that people who are larger don’t work out and don’t work hard to stay healthy as well because “healthy” DOES NOT EQUAL “skinny”.

comments.text:
Okay, so about TikTok1: I am not a professional, but as someone who has been on and off the fitness journey, I can confidently say that what that woman advised is nice when you have nothing better to do. You're not gonna see quicker process or anything. Three tips I wanna give that will actually be important for a successful, healthy fitness journey especially in the gym. 1. Focus on your form ; 2. Make breathing a part of your exercise routine; 3. Focus on actual rest. 

Skip this Monday, Wednesday, Friday-craze because it's neither realistic if you have a real, normal life nor is it healthy. Because what happens on a Monday? You train full intensity, then your muscles are sore, as they are from working out. You give them ONE day to rebuild themselves just to tear them apart again on Wednesday, then do the same until Friday and rinse in repeat with only two days rest over the weekend. Plus, you're gonna probably work on Monday to Friday, or go to school or anything of such sorts that might include a lot of walking or put strain on your legs another way like sitting a lot. 

I am pretty sure your body is not going to recover muscles quicker just because you train more often. The pain fades quicker sure, but your muscles will most likely not repair themselves faster. It's far more sustainable if you go once a week for a couple of hours and hold a good form, breathe properly during the exercise, drink enough water and rest enough, which means: Not going every second day into the gym. To be honest, it's also going to kill your motivation to continue going to the gym if you stress yourself too much about going as often as you can into the gym. Take it easy, more is not always better :)

Natural flavors label & artificial dyes are legitimately something to watch out for specifically. Everything else she listed are normal ass chemicals in natural foods. Dextrin is a thing that is technically processed, but it's via heating up starches like corn usually with acid, so like it may be mildly questionable if it's super high up on the list, but it usually never is since it's just a thickening agent.
But even w/ the dyes, there's 3 specific dyes that are banned in the EU that aren't banned in the US which can cause stomach problems to flare up e
Esp if it's a candy w/ a shit ton of that specific dye. Nothing helped my IBS calm down as much as avoiding those specific food dyes lmfao. Natural flavors is only problematic b/c of how nondescript it is & how many different things can be just labelled as natural flavors, but as far as I know, there's nothing that "dangerous" abt them either.

Either way though, it's good to check ingredients lists & like look stuff you don't know up on trustworthy, scientific sites & if you like some things that have those "questionable" ingredients, that's fine too, just handle it according to what your needs are.
Honestly, all you really need to know is its status in the EU since they mostly just ban ingredients that have some studies linking them to possible problems & they can overdo it, so if it's like not even on their weird ingredient watchlist, chances are it's perfectly fine.

Edit: the EU also just is usually more quick to ban ingredients than the FDA

comments.text:
Those pregnancy "fear mongering" or "self-inflicted mindset" blabbers drive me nuts. 
Firstly, everyone has different experiences through pregnancy, no pregnancy is the same and thats not just true for different women but also having multiple pregnancies. Trying to claim that cravings during pregnancy is a mindset is the dumbest thing I've ever heard. A lot of what that woman and others like her, blaming it all on mindset and failing to understand and admit that its the body natural response for demanding more nutrients for yourself and the little human growing inside you... it really shows the stupidity of their mindset 🤦‍♀️

It annoys me when they talk about pregnancy, like all women have the same pregnancy, or because they have a "smooth" pregnancy with no complications or normal pregnancy issues that occur. Going on that other women are just overreacting, lying, weak mindset, its all her fault, etc. I've got two children, and both pregnancies had similar issues and other issues that I had with one but not the other. Both times I couldnt stomach any food or drink,  I couldn't even hold down water. Even when trying to eat and drink tiny portions, I would still be throwing it up, I was a skeleton with a baby bump until about 7months and then all of a sudden I could finally eat with out spewing up my guts. My 2nd pregnancy I was extremely exhausted, all the time. I never had an enough energy to wake up, or going to the bathroom, etc, even after a good nights sleep. During a checkup got blood work done and found out my Iron levels were dangerously low to the point I could bleed out since my hemoglobin was sooooo low. Which means not enough oxygen getting through the body, thin blood that wouldn't clot. I urgently had to get an iron infusion. 

The point is, all pregnancies are different for the same person and and other women, natural pregnancy bodily responses like cravings are NORMAL, trying to claim that so many normal things is because you are weak minded is such a terrible thing to push, trying to claim such things is completely irresponsible and may cause women to believe the garbage they spout and not seek advice from their midwife or doctor believing that all in their head, especially when it could be a sign of something serious. If you feel or believe something is wrong or doesn't feel right go seek medical advice ASAP and push for testing, or whatever, but never feel like you are wrong and you shouldn't bring up any concerns or issues with a medical professional. Its better to notify and find out nothing is wrong, rather than ignore it and turns out it was something serious and only when things go badly do you seek medical advice but by that stage its usually too late.

comments.text: I thought this would be something interesting to point out- in my college biological anthropology class we recently talked about the impact of the agricultural revolution on health. It’s counterintuitive but the ag revolution is actually associated with several health issues increasing. For example, anemia became increasingly common and it can be identified by porotic hyperostosis ( porous bone tissue on the skull due to marrow overproduction) in skeletal remains. This occurs when children experience malnutrition and develop anemia as a result. Enamel hypoplasia is also more common in skeletal remains from after the ag revolution even though it is caused by disrupted growth due to malnourishment and physiological stress. Another cool thing is that cavities drastically increase during the ag revolution because certain crops like corn were high in sugar content. It doesn’t matter if you literally grow everything yourself with absolutely no processing or “scary chemicals”. There is no way to be healthy while following all this crazy advice.

comments.text:
The second attorney said exactly what I was thinking. The "influencer" didn't prevent her from seeing the scans or force her to forego treatment. The young woman decided to do these things based on the advice of some non-educated stranger on social media. That said, giving medical advice when you are not medically trained is generally not legal, either. Freedom of speech does not mean freedom from consequences for harmful non-protected speech. The same should also go for the SovCit crowd. Giving bad legal advice is also illegal. I personally think anyone who spreads misinformation that breaks the law should face consequences, regardless of whether they are the "influencer" or just some idiot reporting their nonsense. Even so, people have been buying "snake oil" for a long time, and hope-scamming is not new. It even sometimes happens in the medical field. 

On a personal note, I've been sick for a very long time (about 3 decades of acute illness, another decade and a half of less severe illness), and I've had numerous doctors promise me things they can't deliver, and even more so from homeopathy, essential oils, and just poorly-educated but well-intentioned neighbors or friends. About a year ago, a psychiatrist at a hospital told me that all the medical issues I've had since my own days as a teenager, all the pain and lack of function and falling down, would magically vanish if I just, and I quote, "change my frame of mind". The hope-scamming is everywhere. YOU have to choose who to listen to based on principles of truth and empirical evidence. If a doctor promises you that something will be fine and you'll recover and you don't, then do NOT believe them the next time they lie and say you'll be fine after the same type of procedure. If a social media influencer tells you that their miracle cure will cure you, ask questions and do your due dilligence. If you don't, you might end up dead.  That's on every one of us. We need to stop solely blaming the liars and con artists and expecting people to try to see the difference between truth and nonsense.

What the procecutor says is correct, but just because someone is legally an adult does not mean they are immune to emotional manipulation. A child and a fully grown woman in their 40s are both susceptible to lies. If someone were to hand either of them candy and tell them it was a free sample they'd both accept. If they were handed something more suspicious like an open drink perhaps the woman would hesitate and say no but that is not because shes a legal adult. Its easy to agree with the point being made because it is a logical point indeed, for someone to take responsibility for ones own choices and actions, especially from the point of view of someone who is completely unaffected by the emotional strain and manipulation of the issue itself. I lost my aunt to cancer 25 years ago due to an incredible fluke in the way her cancer developed.  She was being treated for IBS and the colonoscopy she had undergone 4 months earlier came back clean.  She went in for surgery to deal with a bowel blockage and was under for six hours.    During the surgery, they removed her uterus, both ovaries, a kidney, over ten feet of her small intestine, part of her large intestine  but didn't touch the seven they could see in her liver because they were out of time.   The bowel cancer didn't show up on the colonoscopy because the tumors started on the outside of the bowel and then grew in--a one in ten million occurrence.  She went in for surgery in August and died just after 12:00 AM Christmas morning.  You have to know that Aunt Ruth was a medical technician; she made informed decisions about her medical treatment up until the end of her life--and she donated her body to science so more could be learned about the progression of cancer in the human body.  

 While my aunt was dealing with her cancer I went in for my first ever mammogram where they found a mass of.5mm on my chest wall.  They couldn't identify it from the mammogram or a series of followup ultrasounds so they biopsied it the day after Christmas.  The biopsy came back Invasive Ductal Carcinoma, Early Stage One.  I had a lumpectomy with radiation followup and took tamoxifen for 15 years. I was told there was a 3% chance of the cancer coming back and they only placed it that high because I was only 41.  Five years ago, a second lump showed up in the same spot--also Invasive Ductal Carcinoma, Stage One.  As of the needle biopsy last month, it hasn't changed in any way except size.  The 1mm lump is now .5mm.  What gets me is that when I first found this second lump I was accosted by a woman at the Cancer Center who insisted the doctors would just make me sicker, essentially what was being promoted by the influencer in this episode of L&O.  When she wouldn't leave me alone I asked the receptionist to call hospital security.   Security showed up with police backup.  Turns out she couldn't legally be on hospital grounds unless she was a patient.    AND SHE KNEW IT!     She just didn't care about the law.

comments.text:
The sad thing is that while this issue is not unfortunately new it has become increasingly prevalent as years have gone by.

People who believe in various forms of alternative medicine have existed since modern medicine. And while in some cases, they do make good arguments unfortunately arguments do not equal results. Some of the biggest problems at least in my opinion are not so much the social media influencers, and all that stuff but it’s the people that seem to have it in their head that faith will heal them.

There’s actually ironically an episode of the show Family Guy of all things where Lois meets a young couple with a son roughly around the same age as Stewie. However, she learns very quickly that their son is dying of cancer. However, the young boys parents think that faith and the Lord will be the ones to help him. And while there’s nothing wrong with believing in God and all that stuff, unfortunately you can’t use that as a crutch to justify allowing somebody to just suffer. Now, some people have argued that doing that is the only way to make it work and all that stuff. But in reality, I disagree completely. While I support religious freedom, and I think that everybody should be allowed to have their own beliefs, I am of the firm conviction that there are certain times where you need to put your own beliefs aside and instead focus on science and proven methods rather than faith or conjecture and stuff like that.

I’ve actually been of the firm belief also that influencers be a social media or otherwise should be required by law to basically give out a disclaimer saying that you know, they are not licensed in these kinds of things.

Like for instance, just because I took a few classes and stuff on military history and all that does not make me an expert in armored warfare. Just like how it doesn’t matter if you’ve read one or two books on cancer management or something. This does not make you an expert on what people should and shouldn’t do.

And unfortunately, people nowadays, especially younger people seem to be far more willing to accept things at face value nowadays.

Now, when it comes to influencers and stuff involving things like medical things and such, unfortunately, they tend to be kinds of people that basically have figured out how to make it so that the affected person is essentially hearing what they want to hear. Unfortunately, though this does not equal out to you know good things happening.

Again, there’s nothing wrong with having your own beliefs. And there’s nothing wrong with discussing those beliefs with like-minded people. But attempting to make it so that essentially everybody should do that is not a good idea.

The rant itself is logical. Why he is using it however is manipulative. The attacking comments he referred to were questioning things like "how mass air-conditioning makes you stronger when ancestors had to withstand the cold." Instead of defending his logic or further elaborating on his understanding of ancestors; the Liver-King decided to attack the question. It is far easier to attack others perspectives then it is to stand, and defend what oneself believes in.

That response was by design made for on-lookers to look at the attacker, and not the defender. A glass-cannon approach to public eyes. Due to the one-sided nature of YouTube conversations you just need to push eyes onto the other, and oneself by default wins. No one is going to look for the comments that may not exist for a retort.

Lastly, there are very good odds the original comment agrees that to achieve more, one must have the mettle to be willing to earn it. That view however is irrelevant to the question. comments.text: I tried Carnivore for 30 days. I had a very different experience. I had no bathroom issues and no gas issues. Going to the bathroom happens less as your body is utilizing everything you eat. I think people who eat too much fat have bathroom issues. Actually all gas went away for me. Mental clarity was amazing. My dentist noticed my gums and teeth improved significantly. I lost 30 pounds in 30 days and did not feel hungry. I am 6'3 and my weight went from 240 to a lean 210. You do need to meal prep. Eating out I did not find difficult. I ate 2 ribeye steaks a day and if I felt like I needed something more, I fried a few eggs. Your tastes buds improve. I never got bored of steak and eggs. Everything was a positive, but if you workout hard, like I do, you never get a pump due to no sugar/carbs in your system, and I did have less energy while working out, but a small amount less. I did not feel like it was possible to build muscle on this diet. This is great for getting lean and staying lean. I did add fruit to my diet after 30 days, before and after my morning workout. A huge improvement. I gained only 5 pounds back with the fruit and with the fiber from the fruit, got back to a more regular daily routine regarding the bathroom. 7 days on carnivore is not long enough to feel the benefits especially if you have caffeine and sugar withdrawals, which I luckily did not but I was already on a low carb diet for years. If you try this diet, start slow, go low carb first, then go all in, but do not over do it on the fat. Stick to steaks, ground beef is not filling like a steak and you can consume more fat in one meal with ground beef vs eating 1 steak.

comments.text:
Did you ever give this diet a retry? 1 week is only enough to experience basically the negative effects of the diet. Especially if it is your first time doing it. The headaches are caffeine withdrawal. You can drink black coffee on the diet but I think you would be surprised how much you actually do not need it once you were on the diet for 2 weeks. And that brings me to my main point, 2 weeks is the sweet spot for when you really start experiencing the positive side effects of this diet. The explosive #2’s are usually gone by this time and you only go # 2 like once every other day max and theres like nothing even there. That is not because you are backed up, it is because your body is literally using and absorbing 95% of what you are eating. This is actually extremely beneficial to your health, more # 2 means more waste intake. At week 2 is when you also would really start to experience the laser sharp focus, mental clarity and the steady energy throughout the day. You sleep better, wake up feeling more energized. You have to start viewing food as fuel when you are on this diet. Normal diet = E87, Carnivore diet = E97, higher octane. It is the best energy, besides Jack3d, that I have ever experienced. 

Now for what you ate. Yes you can eat whatever animal products you want but I recommend sticking to strictly beef and you have to salt it probably at least twice as much as you did. Also eggs and bacon are great and just a little cheese allowance to break up the monotony. The first time I tried carnivore diet I too messed up and thought I should eat some chicken and turkey and maybe even some fish, I quickly learned just how inadequate these meats are on their own. Beef is the most nutrient dense food in the world and has such a broad array of the vitamins and minerals you need. As for vitamin C, I hate to tell you but you need to get more direct sunlight on as much of your skin as possible. Few people can actually achieve normal levels of vitamin C from food or supplements because our bodies just do not really do a good job of absorbing it. At your body weight I would recommend at least 4 eggs for breakfast but if you can do 6 that is great. Then I would be eating at least 1 pound of beef and load it with salt and do not be afraid to add a good amount of butter to the steak and/or the eggs. Fat is your energy source on this diet. As for snacks go you can find healthy meat snacks but they are a little pricey but there are some jerkys and pepperoni that I have to found to be good and healthy. 

I know you probably won’t read this essay but I would love to see you give this diet a real try for 30 days. I guarantee by the end of it you will be contemplate coming off of the diet and going back to normal energy and you will surely be able to tell the viewers how great the positive effects of this diet feels. 

I do the carnivore diet once a month during my sober october challenge as a reset for my gut and mind. Started out as just a sobriety challenge that I did with my friends years ago. But they all said it was too easy for me to do sober october because all I have to stop is drinking and they had other things they had to quit for the month so I said how about I do the carnivore diet with it? They never thought I would do it. One to two weeks into my first try at it and I didnt think I was going to make it either but thats when I really did my research and found out all these things that I am telling you, eating stuff other than beef, eggs, bacon, not adding enough salt for example. Also your body/mind will try to trick you into thinking you will die if you do not eat a carb of some kind, this is normal, this is carb withdrawal and just like withdrawal from drugs carb and caffiene withdrawal can be brutal but every year I do the carnivore diet the negative side effects decrease and the positive side effects increase. Last year when I did it I experienced what we call the carnivore flu for only the first 3 days and not severe at all and the rest of the month I felt great and coming off of the diet I find myself eating much less overall, much less junk food and missing the carnivore diet.

comments.text:
OK, dude the lethargy was mostly caffine withdrawal but also a bit of carb withdrawal. 

On the vitamin c, organ meats like liver actually have decent amounts.

On the bathroom situation, you did eat any yogurt, milk keifer, or have any acv in your water. The fermented foods are essential to avoid gut issues. Dairy would have helped the brown firehose btw. 

The version of carnivore you did was a variation of the lion diet which is the most restrictive version. True lion diet is beef, beef organs, salt, water only. 

Also ways to created variety on carnivore are carnivore breads or carnivore pizza. 2 ingredient carnivore flatbread bread is made by blending cottage cheese with eggs. Spread on a cookie sheet lined with parchment and bake. This works for wraps or as tortilla replacement.  

For bread id use a square baking dish greased up. Shredded mozzarella,  egg, blended with cottage cheese,  salt, baking powder, maybe add whole egg powder in place of flour. Pour in baking pan and bake. Makes 4 slices. I made this then made pulled pork sandwiches where I used cheddar instead of BBQ sauce. 

Yes, I did carnivore.  Did it 30 days behind ibsd. Lots of info say it can heal conditions like that. For me it didn't but it did fix the massive gas and bloating. The brown forehose, not so much. Re adding fiber through fruit and veggies did that.

Also easiest way to go carnivore is start with keto. Carnivore by definition is a ketogenic diet. Keto is essentially a variation of carnivore. Carnivore is as close to zero carbs as you can get. They get carbs from things like dairy, certain organ meats, fish, shellfish, cephalapods like octopus or squid. So some get like zero to 5 g carbs a day, others 10-20. Keto with fruit and veggies is usually maximum 20g carbs a day. And even there there is variation between otc version that counts net carbs and prescription grade that only counts total. Also there is high fat or high protien, and high fat therapeutic keto. The therapeutic version is used for mental health and epilepsy that doesn't respond to medications.  Same with mental health, especially schizophrenia.  

Yes, I've done both keto and carnivore.  Did keto nearly 2 years including a month stint of carnivore.  Did it primarily because of hashimotos abd its effects on my health including reactive hypoglycemia.  Carnivore was specifically to treat my at the time undiagnosed ibsd. 

Yiu did carnivore as restrictive as possible, and went from a more standard diet to carnivore.  No wonder everything went tits up my dude. That was dumbass idea.

comments.text:
Grilling meat creates A.G.E.s which causes colon cancer.
Grilling meat can significantly increase the level of advanced glycation end-products (AGEs) compared to uncooked meat. AGEs are compounds formed when proteins or fats react with sugars, and they are associated with various health concerns, including aging, diabetes, and heart disease. High temperatures and dry heat during grilling, broiling, and searing accelerate AGE formation. 
Here's a more detailed explanation:
AGEs in Foods:
AGEs are naturally present in foods, especially animal-derived ones. However, cooking methods like grilling significantly increase their levels. 
Grilling and AGEs:
High temperatures and dry heat during grilling create conditions that promote the formation of AGEs. 
Health Concerns:
High levels of AGEs have been linked to various health problems, including diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and even Alzheimer's. 
Minimizing AGEs:
To reduce AGE formation during grilling, you can:
Grill at lower temperatures: Grilling at low temperatures, below 180°C, can reduce AGE formation. 
Use marinades: Marinades can help reduce AGE formation by creating a protective layer on the meat. 
Avoid charring: Charred surfaces are high in AGEs. 
Other Cooking Methods:
Poaching, boiling, baking, and lightly sautéing are generally recommended as they produce lower levels of AGEs.

I'm on day 13 and I've never had an issue staying on it. I started by going to McDonalds at about 1am and just getting 5 1/4lb patties only. it was a lot more food than I realized but after eating it I felt full until the next day around lunch. ever since I haven't been hungry and I stopped all snacking, just because I’m not hungry with this diet. it's really weird...  I work nights and I would normally grab a small bag of candy or chocolate to snack on while working... now I don’t do that at all, although this week I did feel a lil bit hungry, so I bought a bag of beef jerky and had a couple of pieces, it cured the craving and was fine the rest of the night... I don’t have a scale at the hotel so I don’t know if I'm down any weight but I do notice I can bend over and put my shoes on a lot easier, plus it's easier to take care of the back side after a number two, if you catch my drift... I really don’t see myself getting off this diet because it is really easy, and cheaper than eating out... I spent $35 on three steaks and two pieces of salmon, it will last me at least three days. I figure I spend $15-20 on one meal from fast food, so I'm saving a ton of money on food.... hopefully this will help someone, if I can do this, so can you... stay positive and when you get the craving for a snack, its ok to have some beef jerky or similar.... much love to all
one side note I should add.... when you start to eat this much meat, your jaw will be hurting fist couple of days, remember, this is real food and your not used to this much chewing....

Homocysteine is an amino acid produced when the body metabolizes methionine, an essential amino acid found in protein-rich foods (especially meat).

Normally, homocysteine is converted to cysteine or back to methionine using B-vitamins (B6, B12, folate).

High levels of homocysteine (hyperhomocysteinemia) are associated with:

Endothelial dysfunction (damage to blood vessel lining)

Increased clotting risk

Atherosclerosis

But over time, your risk goes up, because of the oxidative stress of eating meat; and what it does do your digestive system.

I did the carnivore diet as a challenge for myself for 3 months because it’s easier for me to lose weight if I make it more like a game. People at work knew I was dieting and would ask me what diet I was doing. I would straight up tell them “I’m doing carnivore, it’s horrible don’t do it. If you do do it, add some keto bread and tortillas a couple times a week.” 
I lost most of the weight I was hoping to, stopped when I still had maybe 15 lbs left, gained weight back, and now I’m just eating better food in general. I feel like it was a good way to reset my body so I’m not craving carbs and sugar all the time, but it’s so BORING. 

I like eating meat now though and I have it with every meal, and I was even craving vegetables and fruit while on the diet. I’m in the middle of completely reworking my diet so I don’t have to do such restrictive things to lose weight and keep the weight off. I’m eating mostly vegetables, some fruits, protein with every meal (or so), and only one or two carbs a day. I used to almost exclusively eat carbs and cheese. Feels much better not doing either of the extremes lol
